biodiversity_overview.text: 2,899 GBIF occurrence records for 48 tracked species are attributed to Puducherry, spanning 1835-2026.
2,778 of these records (95.8%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 19, Magnoliopsida 12, Mammalia 4, Actinopterygii 4, Testudines 3, Squamata 3, Amphibia 2, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 6 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Golden Oriole (460), Indian Pond-heron (335), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (303), Indian Pitta (287), Indian Roller (253).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 65 in 2016 to 84 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 0.72% of Puducherry's area (2 areas intersect the state).
8.4% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (232 of 2,778); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Ash Tree (0.36), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Common Cat Snake (0.35), Bulletwood (0.30).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Puducherry (equal-weight reference): cell near 11.625N 79.875E (overall rank 7, median rank across weightings 15).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 0 km2 (0.09% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

0.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (5.96% of the 2000 extent; 0.73% in 2015-2024, rank 16 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2001 (0.01 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 6.37% of land and population density is 2,932.3 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
100% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
